issues.source_quote: Нет, шуба подождёт. Я считаю, главное - это поглядеть мир!
issues.translation_quote: Otherwise it's just work, work...
issues.justification: The tourist's line is mistranslated in places and the banter is flattened; more importantly 'Giprorybа, the fisheries institute' adds an explanation not in the source and leaves a stray Cyrillic character in the name.

issues.translation_quote: Fris Street, Fish Street, - The "Chikanuk" pharmacy...
issues.justification: The passage is a deliberate half-mangled foreign-sounding phrase ('рыбна улица') that is the cue for the password scene; the translation 'Fish Street' erases the broken-language effect.

issues.translation_quote: Time to go, toorist! Don' need... Go...
issues.justification: Odd dialect rendering ('Don' need') does not match the source's mock-foreign speech and sounds incoherent.

issues.translation_quote: Dahm eet
issues.justification: The foreigners' accented mispronunciation of the password is rendered as nonsense 'Dahm eet' inconsistent with the earlier 'Damn it' password; the comedy of mangled 'Чёрт побери' is blurred and the password logic becomes confusing.

issues.source_quote: Упал, выругался... Чёрт возьми! Ух, прости, "Чёрт побери!"
issues.translation_quote: Blast it! Oops, sorry, "Damn it!"
issues.justification: The joke depends on Gesha slipping into the wrong variant of the password phrase; 'Blast it'/'Damn it' lose the near-identical wording that makes the slip matter.

issues.source_quote: Как говорит наш дорогой шеф, в нашем деле гланое - этот самый реализм!
issues.translation_quote: As our dear chief says, in our business the main thing is this here realism!
issues.justification: 'this here' makes a rustic voice that does not match the original's mockingly pompous quotation of the chief; recurring catchphrase is also inconsistently rendered across the film.

issues.translation_quote: Kozodoev ... Kozlodoev... Kozodoev! Kozlodoev!
issues.justification: The running gag of the boss mangling Kozodoev's name (kozel/kozlodoy = 'goat-milker', an insult) is untranslated and unexplained; an English reader loses the joke.

issues.translation_quote: Nelson!
issues.justification: Replacing Kutuzov (the one-eyed general) with Nelson is a creative substitution, but 'Nelson' is also associated with a missing eye and the cultural reference is changed without need; acceptable but the earlier mention of the eye is lost since 'eye' is only addressed later.

issues.source_quote: Кто возьмёт билетов пачку, тот получит... Водокачку!
issues.translation_quote: Buy your tickets by the batch, and you'll win... A water tower to match!
issues.justification: Adequate rhyme, but 'water tower' misrenders водокачка (pumping station) and the verse is the lottery slogan parody; minor meaning shift weakens the joke.

issues.translation_quote: Have you got your weapon? The psychic one...
issues.justification: 'Psychic' means clairvoyant; the source means psychological (scare) weapon, as clarified later. Mistranslation of a key joke.

issues.source_quote: Вы ко мне приедете. Если мы Вам будем нужны… Я вызываю такси на своё имя.
issues.translation_quote: If we need you… You'll come to me. If you need us… I call a taxi in my name.
issues.justification: The roles are scrambled: the colonel is the one who explains; in the source the second sentence is the officer calling a taxi in his own name (Gorbunkov's), but the translation attributes it to the wrong party, confusing the protocol that is later plot-relevant.

issues.source_quote: Ксива? Паспорт... готов! Хаза? ... Клиент? ... Гонорар?
issues.translation_quote: Papers? ... Hideout? ... Mark? ... Cut?
issues.justification: Underworld slang is rendered reasonably, but 'Mark? Mm... Front... Profile...' and 'Cut? Here!' lose the gesture-based dialogue; also 'Just vun tablet' and "I 'eard" are unmotivated accents that do not appear in the source.

issues.translation_quote: Just vun tablet...
issues.justification: Invented German accent not present in the source (the character speaks plain Russian with a comic 'таблэтки'); creates an inconsistent character voice.

issues.source_quote: Не виноватая я! Он сам пришёл!
issues.translation_quote: Ain't my fault! He come by hisself!
issues.justification: Heavy non-standard English dialect overshoots the source's mildly colloquial speech and clashes with the character's earlier voice.

issues.source_quote: Нет, на это я пойтить не могу!
issues.translation_quote: No, that I ain't goin' along with!
issues.justification: The source's rustic ungrammatical 'пойтить' is a fake-peasant touch, but the English dialect is again too heavy and sounds American.

issues.source_quote: куй железо, не отходя от кассы!
issues.translation_quote: strike while the iron's at the till!
issues.justification: The idiom blend is calqued in a way that is awkward but approximates the joke; 'at the till' is acceptable, though the gag is only partly preserved.

issues.translation_quote: Are you in amateur theatricals?
issues.justification: 'Самодеятельность' means amateur performance (talent shows) and is later used by the colonel; 'no amateur theatricals' with the colonel's phrase 'без самодеятельности' (no improvising) mistranslates the idiom's second sense.

issues.translation_quote: toilette, of the outhouse type
issues.justification: 'Toilette' is an odd spelling and the register is off for the deliberately bureaucratic 'туалэт, типа сортир'.

issues.translation_quote: Everything like we agreed, it should be.
issues.justification: Garbled English with an unmotivated inversion; the source is a simple dialect statement.

issues.translation_quote: Quick we take off the cast, and we scram!
issues.justification: Ungrammatical word order not natural English speech.

issues.translation_quote: Always ready, I am!
issues.justification: 'Увсегда готов' (Pioneer motto parody) is rendered with Yoda-like syntax, which introduces an unrelated pop-culture echo.

issues.translation_quote: feer tree
issues.justification: 'Feer tree' is an unexplained misspelling of 'fir tree' used to imitate the character's accent, inconsistent with later 'fir tree'.

issues.translation_quote: Hotel Atlantic ... Hotel Atlantica
issues.justification: The hotel name is shifted between 'Atlantic' and 'Atlantica' in the translation, reproducing a source inconsistency without clarity.

issues.translation_quote: Didn't you read it in Nedelya, the home and family section
issues.justification: Nedelya is left untranslated with no cue that it is a Soviet weekly newspaper; reference is opaque to English readers.
